data_sources: The standard genetic code (universal, with minor documented exceptions)
Trifonov, Gene 261:139-151 (2000): consensus chronological order over 60 independently published methods

tests.test: V3.1 single-base-change codon neighbours encode physicochemically more similar amino acids than chance
tests.interpretation: Amino acid pairs reachable from one another by a single base substitution in the standard genetic code are, on average, closer in hydrophobicity/volume space than a randomly chosen pair of amino acids, and this could not be reproduced by randomly reassigning amino acids to the same codon structure in 2000 shuffles at the observed effect size. This is the real-data fingerprint of Theorem 'Substitution tolerance': the mutational channel through which local substitutions occur is structured so that the substitutions it makes physically available are preferentially the low depth-cost ones.

tests.test: V3.2 codon degeneracy anti-correlates with structural complexity and with late Trifonov recruitment rank
tests.interpretation: Codon degeneracy (a real, fixed property of the standard genetic code) is negatively correlated both with the number of heavy atoms in a residue's side chain and with the independently published Trifonov consensus order of recruitment into the code, and both correlations are stronger than expected under label permutation at conventional significance. Structurally simple, early-recruited residues are exactly the residues Corollary 'The encoded set is a recurrence statistic' predicts should be reachable by the largest number of independent synthetic routes, and the genetic code's own redundancy structure, established on entirely independent grounds, shows the corresponding signature.

tests.test: V3.3 earliest-recruited residues are structurally the simplest
tests.interpretation: Consensus recruitment rank (lower = earlier) correlates positively with heavy-atom count, i.e. earlier-recruited residues have fewer heavy atoms, and this relationship survives label permutation at conventional significance. This is the direct real-data signature of Theorem 'Recurrence is required for a shared category': the residues most likely to be independently rediscovered across unconnected synthetic routes, and hence to cross the recurrence threshold earliest, are the structurally simplest ones, exactly as observed.
